passage:
A new classmate, Ravi, brought lunch that smelled different from what other students usually ate. Some students looked at it curiously, but no one said anything.
During lunch, one student asked, "What is that" His voice sounded rude, though he did not mean to be unkind.
Ravi looked uncomfortable. Then their teacher said, "Food can be a good way to ask about culture, but we need to ask with respect."
The next day, Ravi brought a small extra piece for anyone who wanted to try. Several students liked it.
Later, other students shared their family foods too.
The class learned that difference can make people feel lonely or welcomed. The question is how others respond to it.
